jobs.title: Child and Family Services Internship (Summer 2027) at Nebraska Department of Health & Human Services
jobs.description: Employer: Nebraska Department of Health & Human Services Expires: 11/20/2026 Our Child and Family Services Internship will learn how our Child and Family Services Specialist serve some of our most vulnerable populations. If you are currently enrolled in a college or university, and require an internship to complete course work, take a look at this opportunity! We have opportunities at many of our local DHHS offices across the State.Onsite Locations Include: Omaha, Lincoln, Scottsbluff, Chadron, Nebraska City, Norfolk, South Sioux City, Hastings, Grand Island, Kearney, York, Seward, Fremont, Ogallala, and More. Application Review: March 1st, 2027 Application Deadline: March 26th, 2027 Interns will shadow our Child and Family Service Specialist to gain hands on experience. CFSS roles are rewarding, yet challenging, as they provide opportunities, services, and programs that promote a healthy, safe, and stable environment for children/youth in our communities with their caregivers. CFSS work closely with families that need child welfare intervention because of abuse and/or neglect. CFSS will sometimes work with the legal system toward permanency goals. Case managers are trained on resources necessary to help children and families heal from trauma in their lives, and on the importance of promoting community safety. In Children & Family Services, we aim to provide the least disruptive services when needed, for only the amount of time necessary to give children the opportunity to succeed, live with dignity and respect and help families care for themselves. This will result in healthier families and safer, more prosperous communities. Child & Family Services Interns may learn the basics in the following job duties:Advocate for families.Respect the individuality of each child and family served.Respect each child’s family and culture.Implement family-centered practice principles into case management to ensure the inclusion of children and families in the decision-making processes that impact their lives.Promote normalcy in the lives of children in care.Adhere to principles and procedures of Structured Decision Making as a tool that will support keeping children and families safe.Utilize evidence-based practices that focus on least-restrictive and family-centered approaches.Identifies and makes appropriate referrals for formal and informal interventions based on the family’s needs.Write clear, concise, and descriptive reports in a timely manner that will be shared with legal entities and the court system. You have the passion; we have the opportunities – let’s make a difference for Nebraskans. Requirements / QualificationsMinimum Qualifications: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program at an accredited college or university (two-to-four-year institution) OR recently graduated (within one year) from an undergraduate or graduate degree program at an accredited college or university (two-to-four-year institution). Preferred Qualifications: Coursework in social work, psychology, sociology, counseling, human services, mental healthcare, criminal justice, education, or any other closely related field. Application Review: March 1st, 2027Application Deadline: March 26th, 2027

jobs.title: Environmental Education Fellow at Rocky Mountain Conservancy
jobs.description: Employer: Rocky Mountain Conservancy Expires: 11/20/2026 Rocky Mountain Conservancy is excited to offer two seasonal environmental education fellowships that give current students and recent college graduates the opportunity to serve in a national park while exploring careers in environmental education and the nonprofit sector. Each fellowship is unique and tailored to the individual’s skills, interests, and career goals. This is your chance to live and learn in Rocky Mountain National Park, while supporting the Conservancy's efforts in education, stewardship, and conservation! 2027 Fellowship dates: April 14th, 2027 - October 20th, 2027First review of applications: December 1, 2026These fellowships are designed for highly motivated individuals passionate about outreach and education. Successful fellows thrive in a self-directed environment, where there is a balance between Conservancy-assigned and fellow-selected projects. Each fellowship includes: On-the-job training and experience in a variety of environmental education programs and settings Opportunities to develop and lead programs individually and in partnership with both Rocky Mountain Conservancy (RMC) and Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP) teams Housing and utilities are provided at no cost along with a stipend for living expenses Professional development and networking opportunities with park and nonprofit staff As a fellow, you will have the opportunity to build real-world experience in both the nonprofit and public sectors. Our fellowship will help you develop: A deep understanding of the Conservancy’s work and partnerships Knowledge of the region’s natural and cultural history Skills in program planning and delivery, participant communication, and outreach A professional portfolio of education and outreach work products Required Skills: Dedication to environmental and outdoor education, with the ability to lead programs for children, teens, and adults Adept communication skills, both written and spoken, for diverse audiences and using various media Strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to organize ideas and information quickly Demonstrated ability to independently manage long-term projects and complete assignments on time Desire and ability to work both collaboratively and independently Computer experience with Canva and the Microsoft Office suite, including Word and Outlook, preferred Enthusiasm, a warm disposition, and the ability to handle the stresses of working outdoors with diverse groups of program participants Responsibilities: Develop and lead interactive outdoor programs (i.e. pop-up table talks, and educational bus tours) for diverse audiences, including families, youth, and adults Support expert-led Field Institute programsAssist with development, planning, and implementation for a range of Conservancy programs Support RMNP education and interpretation programs, such as school field trips and Jr. Ranger programs Create outreach and promotional materials for Conservancy programs Establish and maintain positive working relationships with RMNP staff and volunteers, as well as with other Conservancy partners, program participants, and community members Assist Conservancy and park staff with outreach events Drive and/or ride in Conservancy-owned vehicles, including the Conservancy’s 15-passenger buses Each position averages 30-40 hours per week, with schedules that vary throughout the fellowship. A full 6-month commitment is required. Fellows are provided with housing (including all utilities) for the duration of their fellowship. Shared housing units are located near Conservancy headquarters in Estes Park, CO, in units operated by Rocky Mountain National Park. Fellows also receive a living stipend of $450/week (paid as $900 every two weeks). Fellows must be eligible to work in the USA and must pass a background check. It is recommended that the candidate be actively pursuing or have recently completed a degree program in environmental education, general education, communication, outdoor recreation/tourism, natural resource management, or similar. In addition, experience volunteering or working with nonprofit organizations and an interest in public outreach and conservation is desired. Visit us online to learn more: https://rmconservancy.org/work-with-us/environmental-education-fellowships/To apply, email your resume, cover letter, and at least three professional references (including phone numbers andemail addresses) to opportunity@RMConservancy.org. In the subject line, specify whether you’re applying for the Outdoor Education Fellowship or the Environmental Education Fellowship.

jobs.title: Food and Beverage Internship @ Bandon Dunes Golf Resort at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort
jobs.description: Employer: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort Expires: 11/23/2026 Ready to see how a great restaurant really runs? As a Food & Beverage Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, you'll work in one of our dining outlets alongside our F&B Manager and Supervisor, learning the side of hospitality guests never see: how a shift gets set up, how a busy dinner service stays on track, and how the team pulls together to make every meal part of a trip of a lifetime. Whether you're studying hospitality or business or have recently graduated, this is your chance to get real, hands-on restaurant operations experience, with people who want to teach you and help you build a career in food and beverage.This internship is for hospitality students and recent graduates. To be considered, you should be currently enrolled in a hospitality management (or related) degree program or have graduated from one within the past year.About Bandon Dunes Golf Resort:Bandon Dunes is a world-class golf resort located on the Oregon Coast near the charming community of Bandon. Guests come to experience golf as it was meant to be at Bandon Dunes' six distinct golf courses. That includes five 18-hole courses, which all rank among the top 16 public courses in the United States, according to Golf Digest. The resort is also home to two 'Courses with a Mission': Bandon Preserve, an award-winning par-3 course, and Shorty's, which opened in 2024. All net proceeds from both courses fund the Bandon Dunes Charitable Foundation, supporting communities along the South Coast of Oregon.Beyond premier golf, guests delight in various dining options at Bandon Dunes’ collection of restaurants. Whether you're looking to enjoy locally sourced, Pacific-Northwest cuisine accompanied by an award-winning wine list or prefer kicking back in a Scottish-style setting with traditional pub fare and local microbrews, there is something for everyone.Working at Bandon Dunes is a dream for golf fans, outdoor enthusiasts, and hospitality professionals alike. The Bandon Dunes team works together to create trips of a lifetime for our guests. We are passionate stewards of our resort, community, and environment. As an endlessly curious group, we ask questions, share ideas, and always look for a better way. With a hard-working attitude, we help guide our guests through their pure golf experience, immersed in Oregon’s natural beauty and away from the demands of daily life.What You'll Do:Help keep service running smoothly. You'll support the F&B Manager and Supervisor during daily shifts, pitching in wherever the team needs you when the dining room gets busy. You'll see firsthand how the people running a shift keep service flowing and standards high.Take care of our guests. You'll greet guests, handle requests, and help sort out concerns with a calm, professional touch. Many of our guests have planned this trip for years, and how their meal goes is a big part of how they remember it.Learn how a restaurant opens and closes. You'll learn the routines behind every shift: setup, breakdown, cash handling, and securing the outlet at the end of the night.Get behind the scenes of operations. You'll help track stock levels and supplies, assist with scheduling and shift coverage, and sit in on department meetings. Bring your ideas. We're always looking for a better way to do things.Learn our wine and beverage program. Bandon Dunes is known for its award-winning wine list. You'll learn about our selections, proper wine service, and how beverages help shape the guest experience.Help hold the line on quality. You'll keep an eye on service standards, food and beverage presentation, and cleanliness, and follow the policies and safety procedures that keep our guests and team safe.What Makes You a Great Fit:You want a career in food and beverage. Maybe you're studying hospitality, restaurant management, or business, or you've recently graduated. Restaurant or customer service experience helps, but it isn't required. What matters most is that you want to learn how restaurants run.You're good with people. You communicate clearly with guests, teammates, and managers, and you enjoy making someone's experience a little better.You stay steady when it gets busy. Service has its rushes. You can keep track of several things at once, stay calm, and notice the details that make a difference.You're a good teammate. jobs.title: City Scout - Miami at Atlys
jobs.description: Employer: Atlys Expires: 11/27/2026 About AtlysOur mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.Travel should feel exciting. Instead, too much of it is still defined by paperwork, uncertainty, and processes that were never designed for travellers.Atlys is changing that.We’re building an AI-first platform that removes friction and uncertainty from travel. To date, we’ve processed visas for 1M+ travellers across 127 countries. But we’re still early.The RoleWe're looking for a City Scout to help build the most reliable database of work-friendly cafes for travellers across the USA.You'll visit cafes across your assigned city, verify information like WiFi quality, internet speed, plug points and overall work-friendliness, and submit accurate data that powers a new Atlys product. Every visit directly improves the travel experience for thousands of users.Hiring in: New York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles.The JobExplore and discover great cafes: Visit assigned cafes across your city, experience them as a customer, and identify places that travellers would genuinely enjoy working from.Collect high-quality on-ground data: Verify key details including WiFi availability, internet speed, passwords, plug points, seating, ambience and overall work-friendliness to ensure the information is accurate and reliable.Contribute to a travel product used by thousands: Capture your observations by completing a short digital survey after every visit, helping build one of the world's most reliable databases of work-friendly cafes.Cover your city efficiently: Plan your visits across assigned neighbourhood clusters to maximize coverage while maintaining consistency and quality.Maintain exceptional data quality: Pay close attention to detail, validate every submission, and ensure the information travellers see on the Atlys app can be trusted.The Ideal CandidateYou’ll likely thrive in this role if you:Are a college student or have a flexible part-time schedule.Enjoy exploring your city and discovering new places.Have strong attention to detail and collect information accurately.Are comfortable travelling independently within your city.Own a smartphone and are reliable, proactive and self-driven.We hire exceptional people for their craft, not travel enthusiasts. We solve hard problems that happen to touch global travel and government infrastructure.Our values shape how we make decisions, work together and build for travelers. The bar is high, the pace is fast, and the way we work is deliberate. Read them before you apply. If this environment energizes you, you’ll probably thrive here. If it doesn’t, it’s better to know that upfront.Come build the intelligence layer for global travel

jobs.title: Foster Youth Internship Program® at Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute Expires: 11/28/2026 Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute’s (CCAI) Foster Youth Internship (FYI) Program® is a competitive national internship for students and recent graduates with lived experience in the US foster care system who are interested in federal policy and advocacy. Participants write a federal child welfare policy report and are placed in the Washington, D.C. legislative offices of Members of the U.S. Congress. Participants will travel to D.C. for the 8 week program over the summer and will be required to live in dormitory-style housing provided by CCAI. The Foster Youth Internship Program® closes to applicants on November 15th, 2026.The Foster Youth Internship Program® (FYI) began in 2003 as an effort to raise awareness to federal policymakers about the needs and unique perspectives of individuals who have experienced the U.S. foster care system. CCAI works with congressional offices to secure a congressional internship for each participant. In addition, CCAI organizes an orientation, advocacy trainings, networking, and various other professional development opportunities. These combined experiences allow the participants to create a policy report that is presented to U.S. Congress, Administration, Department of Health and Human Services, and released to policymakers and advocates across the country. As a result of the program, federal policymakers learn firsthand the experiences of youth in foster care and go on to use their new knowledge to inspire legislative change to federal child welfare policy. Participants benefit both personally and professionally, gaining experience and skills that will bolster their careers for years to come. This is an immersive eight-week, educational, and civic experience in Washington, D.C. with a comprehensive onboarding to ensure participants are well-prepared for effective advocacy and leadership development in the nation's capital. Participants are not considered employees of CCAI nor their congressional office. CCAI provides a monthly stipend during the remote preparatory onboarding (February 1 - May 28) and weekly stipend while in Washington, D.C. (May 31 - July 23), and covers major expenses, such as housing in Washington, D.C., transportation to/from Washington, D.C., and public transportation to/from the congressional office internship. Participants are responsible for some smaller expenses. Interns are required to live in dormitory-style housing assigned by CCAI for the duration of the program and to adhere to the guidance and regulations of the program.Each congressional office placement differs. CCAI does not guarantee that the intern will be assigned projects that are related to child welfare. Office responsibilities will likely include: Open, sort, and deliver mailAnswer phones, greet constituents, run errands, deliver priority letters, and acquire signaturesCopy, file, fax, data entry, and work on small legislative projects Work directly with congressional staff to research issues and compose constituent correspondenceAttend committee hearings, sit in on meetings, attend press conferences, and take notes Provide constituent services and give tours of the U.S. Capitol Attend and assist with congressional briefings and meetings, including various events organized by CCAI The Foster Youth Internship Program® closes to applicants on November 15th, 2026.Please review our eligibility requirements, due dates, and all other necessary info at https://www.ccainstitute.org/programs/view/foster-youth-internship-apply to learn more or join us for our last info session on October 23rd! If you have questions after carefully reviewing this application and the information available on CCAI’ s website about the Foster Youth Internship Program®, please contact Lisette DuFore Benz at lisette@cccainstitute.org or (202) 544-8500 ext. 12.

jobs.title: Community Outreach Facilitator at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 11/28/2026 The Community Outreach Facilitator plays a crucial role in supporting and expanding the Polk County Conservation Community unity Volunteer Program. This position works directly in the field alongside PCC staff and community volunteers, providing on-site guidance and support on community volunteer-assigned projects and at scheduled events that connect community volunteers with meaningful outdoor work. This role is highly field-focused, with an emphasis on being present with community volunteers in natural areas, helping them succeed in their assigned projects, and strengthening community involvement in conservation. One Three-Quarter Time Community Outreach Facilitator will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($16,620) paid out equally over the course of 1200 hours of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon completion ($5,176.50) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. This position is a Three-Quarter Time volunteer, who will serve a minimum of 1200 hours over 39 weeks, serving 39 hours per week. This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Daily TimesThe typical weekly schedule will be established with the selected candidate to ensure they do not exceed 40 hours per week, candidates can expect the typical schedule to fall within Monday through Friday 6:30 AM to 4:30 PM Every service day will include two 15-minute breaks; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degreesA 30-minute lunch period is included with every service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required service hours during the termHours during the week can be flexed to ensure the volunteer has a sustainable workload when a special evening or weekend event is scheduled during a given service week, volunteer will have access to event calendar a minimum of two weeks in advance of the scheduled event Volunteer will serve 1-2 Saturdays per month during their term; most Saturday events take place from 10 AM to 12 PM Volunteer is expected to show up before the start of an event to assist with setup and logistics and to stay after the end of the event to assist with cleanup and inventory of supplies Evenings and weekends are built into the schedule with a minimum of two weeks' notice prior to a volunteer being assigned Listed below are key annual events that occur during the spring, summer, and fall: May | Spring Into Action | Woodland Restoration June | National Trails Day | Trail Construction April, May, June | Tree Planting at identified priority woodland October | Moonlight Seed HarvestThe typical weekly schedule may change to better meet the needs of the Natural Resources Department* Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. TrainingAll volunteers will go through two weeks of intensive in-person training to learn all the skills necessary to complete the volunteer duties outlined below.The Natural Resources Volunteer Outreach Representative AmeriCorps Volunteer will lead community volunteers and actively participate in a variety of natural resources management and conservation activities. The focus of the position is hands-on service, fostering environmental stewardship, and contributing to the overall improvement and preservation of natural habitats through the assistance of community volunteers. The Volunteer Outreach Representative will be responsible for leading community volunteers in executing impactful projects such as invasive species removal, prairie seed harvest, trail maintenance, garden bed maintenance, and tree planting. Volunteers will receive the following training and certifications before service activities begin:Volunteers will complete CPR/AED and first aid certification through Heart Saver online modules and an in-person practical skills testMental Health First Aid trainingVolunteers will participate in a week-long chainsaw handling and maintenance training and pass a in-person practical skills test with full-time Polk County Conservation natural resources staff volunteersIowa Pesticide Applicator Certification in Categories 4 (Core), 2 (Forestry) and 6 (Right of Way)Volunteers must read each designated booklet in order to register for each corresponding category testTesting occurs online and utilizes LockDown Browser application that records video of the tester during the timed tests; personal laptops may be utilized for testing or computers will be available for volunteers to useVolunteers must receive an 80% or better to receive category certificationsVolunteers receive their Iowa Pesticide Applicator’s License once all three category tests are successfully passedNational Wildland Coordinating Group Certifications:S-130 – Firefighter TrainingS-190 – Introduction to Wildland Fire BehaviorThey may also have the opportunity to receive additional certifications in:L-180 – Human Factors in the Wildland Fire ServiceIS-700 – NIMS (National Incident Management System): An IntroductionAll AmeriCorps Environmental Stewards in the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program are required to complete CPR/AED and first aid online modules; Mental Health First Aid training; Iowa Pesticide Applicator tests in Core, 2, and 6; and the National Wildland Coordinating Group online modules of S-130 and S-190 within three weeks subsequent to their official start date. Failure to complete these trainings and certifications in a timely manner will result in a volunteer not receiving integral certifications utilized by the Program. Missing or skipping trainings and certifications could impact the ability of a volunteer to remain enrolled within the Program. jobs.title: Cabin Counselor at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 12/01/2026 Cabin Counselor – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Being a Cabin Counselor is exhausting. It’s messy. It’s challenging. And it’s also one of the most rewarding things you can do with your summer.Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.What We’re Looking For:We want people who:Love working with kidsCan serve as strong, positive role modelsAre ready to lead Are excited to help young people grow in faithDon’t mind unplugging and spending a summer in the woodsWe aren't going to lie, being a camp counselor is incredibly hard work. You’ll be responsible for the daily care and well-being of the campers in your cabin — making sure they eat, sleep, brush their teeth, wear socks, and feel safe. It looks different each week and could mean sitting up with them at night when they're scared of the dark. It means teaching them how to paddle a kayak, supporting them at the rock wall/zip lines, building fires for skillet enchiladas (you’re going to love it), dancing to Grooveship worship and answering their questions about Jesus in Bible It also means picking up a kid when they fall in the dirt, giving them a high five when they finally hit the bullseye in archery, and letting them cover you in mud in the creek. It's all part of walking alongside campers through a week of fun, growth, and faith—and helping give them a summer they'll never forget.At Camp Bear Creek, counselors don’t just supervise- they lead. You’ll gain real world experience in:Leadership and public speakingCurriculum planning and facilitationConflict resolution and creative problem-solving Teamwork across diverse backgrounds. These soft skills are essential in every career field. You’ll also lead a variety of camp activities and work with different age groups- giving you the opportunity to grow into a well-rounded leader. We are also willing to work with you to ensure that this job can be used for internship credit in fields like Education, Public Health, Recreation & Leisure, Youth Services, Psychology and more. However, any student in any field can benefit from a summer camp experience like this. You’ll be part of an incredible team of about 30 college-aged staff from across Iowa, the U.S., and even around the world. We work hard. We play hard. We show up for each other every day. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to grow — and who feel like family by the end of week one. This is more than a job. It’s a ministry, a leadership opportunity, and a summer you’ll never forget. You’ll give this job everything you’ve got — and it will give even more back.So, if you're looking for a summer full of purpose, adventure, community, and growth, don't let this opportunity pass you by. For more information about working at Camp Bear Creek or to apply, visit https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/

jobs.description: Employer: Charles River Laboratories Expires: 12/03/2026 ob Title: Summer 2027 Intern - Post-Doc - BiomarkerFor 75 years, Charles River employees have worked together to assist in the discovery, development and safe manufacture of new drug therapies. When you join our family, you will have a significant impact on the health and well-being of people across the globe. Whether your background is in life sciences, finance, IT, sales or another area, your skills will play an important role in the work we perform. In return, we’ll help you build a career that you can feel passionate about.Job OverviewDoctoral/Post-doctoral Internship essential Functions (The fundamental Duties & Responsibilities of the role (products and services provided/results accomplished) include, but are not limited to, those listed: • Efficiently perform and document all procedures, materials and results in compliance with applicable regulatory standards as applicable (protocols, methods, SOPs, etc.)• Actively communicate and collaborate across operational areas in order to adhere to timelines and produce quality data• Assist and/or execute assigned project with oversight to gain first-hand experience with industry drug development• Assist with the completion of laboratory investigations, assay troubleshooting, quality observations, and problem solving of technical and/or regulatory issues with oversight, as needed• Effectively develop quantitative/qualitative methods/procedures with limited complexity/scope in one operational area with minimal oversight• Develop critical thinking, troubleshooting and time management skills aligned with needs of operational areas• Demonstrate effective communication skills through informal discussions with peers, supervisor, and team• Develop ability to recognize method and/or data issues and communicate them to management to minimize study impact with minimal oversight• Develop knowledge of regulatory and GXP requirements, industry standards and company SOPs within one operational area• Performs all other related duties as assignedThe pay range for this position is $33.00 per hour. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Growth Operations at Tria Federal
jobs.description: Employer: Tria Federal Expires: 12/03/2026 Tria Federal delivers digital services and technology solutions that support the health and safety of veterans, service members and civilians. For two decades, federal agencies have relied on Tria companies to advance their critical missions and modernize their systems, so that they can uphold their commitment to the American people. Today, we are pushing the boundaries of possibility through partnerships and investments in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, developing solutions for the biggest challenges that government will face tomorrow.We are proud to employ and support military veterans who bring mission-first mindset, technical expertise, and leadership qualities that strengthen our work. Veterans, transitioning service members, and military spouses are strongly encouraged to apply.Job Description:Tria Federal (Tria) is seeking driven and ambitious individuals to join our 2027 Summer Internship Program. This full-time opportunity offers a hands-on, impactful work experience tailored to align with your academic and career aspirations. As an intern at Tria, you’ll gain valuable exposure by collaborating with colleagues and engaging with senior executives, all while participating in professional development activities and networking opportunities that enrich your experience.The Growth Operations Intern supports Tria’s Business Development and Growth function by using technology to advance how the team identifies, qualifies, and captures federal business. The intern owns one or more substantive projects, scoped with the mentor at the start of the internship, that apply AI tools, automation, data integration, or analytics to a real operational need within growth operations. Representative projects include building a working application or tool for the BD team, automating a manual BD or capture workflow, improving pipeline analytics and reporting, or connecting data sources that currently operate in isolation. Projects are built using vibe coding, in which the intern describes desired behavior in plain English to an AI coding assistant (Claude, Cursor, or similar) and iterates on the output. No prior development experience is required. The internship is self-directed and build-first: the intern sets the pace, manages research, troubleshoots build challenges, and produces weekly deliverables without day-to-day direction, while drawing on the full breadth of the organization’s resources when the work demands it. Progress is reviewed weekly by the mentor and at formal checkpoints by the mentor alongside a BD colleague with experience in comparable builds. The role applies Tria’s AI- and technology-enabled operating model to the Growth function, converting manual, reactive processes into proactive, data-driven ones that the team can maintain and scale after the intern departs. The ideal candidate is curious about AI tools, writes clearly, works independently, and is interested in how federal business development operates. Responsibilities: Technology Projects for Growth Operations Scope, design, and build one or more projects that apply technology to a real need within Tria’s BD and capture operations, such as an application or tool for the Growth team, an automated workflow, a reporting or analytics capability, or a data integration. Build using vibe coding, describing desired behavior in plain English to an AI coding assistant and iterating on the output until it produces the intended result. Validate data accuracy and structure before building logic on top of it. Troubleshoot build challenges independently before engaging technical staff or other support resources. Data Integration and Pipeline Analytics Work with real pipeline data from Salesforce (Growth Opportunity records) and maintain spreadsheet backups where appropriate. Research and integrate market research and federal data sources (e.g., SAM.gov, USASpending, agency forecasts, GovWin, G2X) and document a data source map for each input a project depends on. Support pipeline reporting and analysis that helps the Growth team prioritize pursuits and track progress. Growth Operations Technology Enablement Apply AI tools (Claude, Cursor, and similar) across Growth workflows, identifying where manual BD and capture tasks can be automated or accelerated. Develop prompt precision as a core skill: the ability to describe a problem with enough clarity and specificity that the AI produces the intended result. Stress-test what is built under realistic conditions and document the findings. Domain Learning and Research Learn Govcon fundamentals, the federal acquisition lifecycle, Tria’s BD approach, and customer communication in direct service of the current project, using provided resources, reference materials, and organizational subject-matter experts. Maintain a vocabulary log of Govcon and BD terms, defined in the intern’s own words. Research market, competitor, and customer information in support of active pursuits as projects require. Documentation and Knowledge Transfer Maintain a documented snapshot of project state at the end of each week (what is live, what is functional, what has been validated), updated without prompting. Draft operational SOPs written for a user who did not build the tool. Assemble a complete handoff package for each project, including the application or tool, SOP, data source map, and supporting artifacts. Deliver a final presentation to leadership with a live demo and a recommendation for the next step toward a production-grade capability. Internal Collaboration Attend a weekly check-in with the mentor, structured around the week’s deliverable and project state. Participate in formal reviews with the mentor and the BD colleague at designated checkpoints. Engage BD professionals, technical staff, senior leaders, and other Tria staff as the work requires. Facilitate team usability testing of what is built and resolve the friction points surfaced. Qualifications: Currently enrolled in, or a recent graduate of, an undergraduate or graduate program in business, public policy, information systems, data analytics, or a related field. No prior coding or development experience required; demonstrated curiosity about AI tools and a willingness to learn by building. Ability to describe problems clearly and precisely in writing; strong written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated ability to work independently, set priorities, and manage a multi-week project to completion. Interest in federal government contracting and business development. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; exposure to Salesforce or another CRM, SAM.gov, or USA Spending is a plus. Must be a U.S. citizen.

Reporting: Compiling findings into clear, concise reports that summarize key insights and recommendations for asset maintenance and improvement. jobs.title: Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 12/05/2026 The Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator plays a vital role in advocating for and enhancing outdoor recreation opportunities within Polk County Conservation. This position focuses on expanding Veteran’s programming, youth mental health initiatives, and enhancing current Equestrian Center program offerings. AmeriCorps Volunteers serving with the Equestrian Center will have dual enrollment in the Youth Mental Health Corps (YMHC) that is a nationwide initiative. Participants gain valuable practical skills through professional trainings and certification programs. The YMHC program is limited to individuals who are between the ages of 18-24; persons outside of that age range are ineligible for enrollment. This position is supportive and preventative in nature, not clinical. Volunteers do not provide therapy, counseling, diagnoses, or independent crisis intervention, nor are they expected to manage mental health emergencies beyond their training and comfortability. Instead, they help connect youth with appropriate staff and resources while contributing to a supportive outdoor environment. Through this service, Volunteers advance Polk County Conservation’s mission by making outdoor recreation and conservation education more accessible and meaningful for local youth, while helping foster the development of social connections and supportive experiences that contribute to the well-being of Polk County residents. One Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($6,270) paid equally over the course of 450 hours of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon successful completion ($1,956.35) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. This position is Quarter-Time; Volunteers will serve a minimum of 450 hours over the course of 32 weeks, serving a minimum of 10 hours/week from January to May and a minimum of 24 hours/week from June to August. This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Volunteer Schedule January to May January program orientation and YMHC trainings Volunteer will spend a minimum of 10 hours/week participating in position-specific orientation and trainings. Some elements of the orientation and training can be completed via teleservice, but requires prior approval from Program Coordinator February program sessions begin: Monday evenings 4pm-8pm; Volunteer will complete YMHC tasks to meet the minimum of 10 hours/week June to August Summer youth programming sessions begin: Monday-Thursday 7am-2pm; 24 hours/week A 30-minute meal break will be allocated to the volunteer if they serve five consecutive hours in one service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required 450 service hours Every service day will include one 15-minute break; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degrees Volunteer may serve during special events that take place on some weekends A minimum of two weeks’ notice will be given to Volunteer prior to the event occurring Volunteer will be allowed to flex hours during the week if there is an event occurring over the weekend to promote a healthy workload * Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. The Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will receive two weeks of comprehensive training focused on the Jester Park Equestrian Center. Volunteers will become familiar with the facility, current equine services offered, current public outreach efforts, basic equine husbandry, fundamentals of speech to communicate with program attendees, and basics of program development. Volunteers will continue to receive on-the-job training outside of the first two weeks to improve their understanding of the changing needs of the public demographic that utilizes the Jester Park Equestrian Center. All participants in the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Youth Mental Health Corps Program that serve around youth or vulnerable adults are required to complete the following trainings: CPR/AED and first aid certification through the American Heart Association via online modules and an in-person practical skills test Mental Health First Aid Iowa DHS Mandatory Reporter Training ACEs 360 Volunteers may select between two YMHC workforce pathways based on their personal career goals. jobs.title: CDC Global Health Laboratory Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/06/2026 Application Deadline1/1/2027 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.CDC Office and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the Office of the Associate Director for Laboratory Science (ADLS) in the Global Health Center (GHC) at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia.The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is one of the major operation components of the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC protects America from health, safety and security threats, both foreign and in the U.S. Whether diseases start at home or abroad, are chronic or acute, curable or preventable, human error or deliberate attack, CDC fights disease and supports communities and citizens to do the same. CDC increases the health security of our nation. As the nation’s health protection agency, CDC saves lives and protects people from health threats. To accomplish its mission, CDC conducts important science and provides health information that protects our nation against expensive and dangerous health threats, and responds when these arise.Research Project: ADLS supports integration and promotion of strong public health laboratory systems in international settings with CDC’s overseas offices, Ministries of Health and other partners. The integration of strong quality public health laboratory systems improves our ability to detect and respond to disease threats where they are to protect Americans. Analysis of CDC’s global public health laboratory activities helps to coordinate efficiencies across the Agency and overseas offices, as well as with our interagency partners. Data are used to improve reporting systems and tools and will impact leadership decisions around disease surveillance, preparedness, and response. This mentored research experience focuses on global public health laboratory systems and their role in disease detection, surveillance, preparedness, and response. You will gain knowledge of approaches used to examine CDC’s global laboratory activities and public health laboratory systems in collaboration with overseas offices, Ministries of Health, and other public health organizations. Research activities may include analyzing and interpreting laboratory program data, examining reporting systems and analytical tools, and learning how scientific findings are communicated to public health audiences.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will have opportunities to:Learn about global public health laboratory systems and CDC’s scientific approaches related to disease detection, surveillance, preparedness, and response.Develop skills in generating, analyzing, and interpreting data and gain knowledge of methods used to evaluate laboratory reporting systems and analytical tools.Learn how laboratory data are synthesized and interpreted to characterize public health trends and contribute to scientific understanding of surveillance, preparedness, response, and recovery.Strengthen oral and written scientific communication skills through mentored learning activities, multidisciplinary research discussions, and opportunities to communicate analytical findings.Gain exposure to public health laboratory research, technical communities of practice, and international laboratory collaboration, and learn how epidemiologic and laboratory information is examined during outbreak preparedness and response activities.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Anne Purfield (aip4@cdc.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: November 2, 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for eleven months, but may be renewed upon recommendation of CDC and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: Stipend rates may vary based on numerous factors, including opportunity, location, education, and experience. If you are interviewed, you can inquire about the exact stipend rate at that time and if selected, your appointment offer will include the monthly stipend rate.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and CDC. Participants do not become employees of CDC, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email CDCrpp@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received a bachelor’s or master’s degree in the one of the relevant fields. Degree must have been received within the past five years.Preferred skills:Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate technical information to diverse audiencesAbility to think critically and analyze findingsExperience synthesizing, summarizing, and presenting information from multiple sources in written reports, presentations, or other communicationsAbility to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teamsStrong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to handle multiple activitiesExperience with data management, analysis, and visualization is beneficialExperience in a laboratory setting is advantageousPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsCitizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree received within the last 60 month(s).

jobs.title: CDC Global Immunization and Polio Eradication Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/06/2026 Description*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.CDC Office and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is one of the major operation components of the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC protects America from health, safety and security threats, both foreign and in the U.S. Whether diseases start at home or abroad, are chronic or acute, curable or preventable, human error or deliberate attack, CDC fights disease and supports communities and citizens to do the same. CDC increases the health security of our nation. As the nation’s health protection agency, CDC saves lives and protects people from health threats. To accomplish its mission, CDC conducts important science and provides health information that protects our nation against expensive and dangerous health threats, and responds when these arise.Research Project: You will participate in a mentored fellowship with CDC’s Global Immunization Division (GID) focused on the scientific and public health approaches associated with global polio eradication. Through interactions with CDC technical personnel, you will learn about strategic, analytical, epidemiologic, and communication approaches used in polio eradication, including preparedness for and response to poliovirus outbreaks. As learning opportunities arise, you may also gain exposure to broader emergency preparedness and response approaches, including those used within CDC’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and Incident Management Structure (IMS).You will learn how technical and regional teams collaborate on global polio eradication activities; gain experience analyzing and synthesizing epidemiologic, programmatic, and outbreak-related information; and develop an understanding of how briefings, updates, and other informational materials communicate scientific findings. You will also strengthen collaboration skills through interactions across CDC programs and gain insight into partnerships involving Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) organizations and U.S. Government counterparts.You may gain mentored research experience related to outbreak preparedness and response, including analysis of outbreak and response data, examination of response-planning approaches, and research on guidance documents and information systems associated with outbreak readiness. Additional learning opportunities may include gaining familiarity with analytical tools and resources used to assess preparedness and observing or participating in educational and research activities related to polio outbreak response alongside experienced epidemiologists and other technical personnel.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will strengthen skills in applied epidemiology, data analysis, global immunization program approaches, outbreak preparedness and response research, and scientific communication. You will gain experience analyzing and interpreting epidemiologic and outbreak-related information, learn how scientific evidence informs public health practice, and develop an understanding of the epidemiologic, analytical, and collaborative approaches used in global polio eradication and emergency preparedness.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Monica Fleming (njl9@cdc.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 11, 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be between January 2027 - September 2027, but may be renewed upon recommendation of CDC and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: Stipend rates may vary based on numerous factors, including opportunity, location, education, and experience. If you are interviewed, you can inquire about the exact stipend rate at that time and if selected, your appointment offer will include the monthly stipend rate.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens, Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR), and foreign nationals. Non-U.S. citizen applicants should refer to the Guidelines for Non-U.S. Citizens Details page of the program website for information about the valid immigration statuses that are acceptable for program participation.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and CDC. Participants do not become employees of CDC, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility, including but not limited to, poliovirus requirements (e.g. immunization, testing prior to laboratory access).Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email CDCrpp@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields. Preferred skills:Graduate-level training or equivalent experience in public health, epidemiology, global health, immunization, infectious diseases, emergency management, or a related field.Experience analyzing epidemiologic, surveillance, programmatic, or operational data.Familiarity with infectious disease prevention, vaccination programs, outbreak response, emergency preparedness, or public health programs.Ability to synthesize complex information into concise briefings, reports, presentations, dashboards, and other decision-support items.Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information to diverse audiences.Ability to collaborate with domestic and international partners, manage multiple priorities, act independently, and adapt to evolving program needs.Stipend$5,439.25 MonthlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree received within the last 60 months or currently pursuing.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Internship - Strategy Intelligence: Service Line Strategy (Graduate Level) at Vizient, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Vizient, Inc. Expires: 12/07/2026 Vizient Intern Program Overview: This program is designed to foster a beneficial relationship and provide growth opportunities for Vizient, our employees, and collegiate students. Since 2000, our summer intern program has provided college undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students with practical experience that exposes them to multiple aspects of a career field and the healthcare industry. This full-time, paid intern program offers an opportunity to accelerate academic learning, apply classroom knowledge, and introduce students to a professional setting. Interns are assigned a supervisor to mentor/develop their business skills, as well as monitor their work experiences. Interns are integral members of the company’s team, setting goals, working toward deadlines, and actively participating in community service projects. The program requires the intern to commit to 10 weeks of participation in all formal training, mentoring, on-the-job learning, and opportunities to interact with senior leaders. Program starts June 1, 2027, and ends August 6, 2027 Pay rate: $25 per hour. About the team and role Vizient’s Strategy Intelligence Team helps health system leaders understand where health care is headed, what it means for their organization, and what to do next. We combine forward-looking perspectives from our subject matter experts with powerful analytics to help members see the implications of what’s coming and make confident decisions. The insights we share with clients span big picture industry topics like the future outlook for finance & payment, ambulatory strategy, digital health & AI in addition to service line intelligence across clinical areas like Cardiovascular, Cancer, Neurosciences, Orthopedics and Pediatrics. As a graduate intern, you will support projects that translate healthcare research and data into practical and actionable takeaways, which could include slide decks, white papers, case studies and strategic frameworks. Your work will include researching and synthesizing industry and clinical trends, analyzing data, and contributing to client-facing materials. You will have opportunities to gain exposure to our clients and members, as well as colleagues across Vizient, and learn about the issues health system leaders face as they plan for growth and navigate industry dynamics. What You’ll Do Support a defined project that addresses a current service-line strategy related question or theme and produces a client-ready deliverable. Conduct industry, policy, market, and organizational research; identify relevant sources; analyze data, and summarize findings for use in publications, presentations, and strategic discussions. Collaborate with service line experts and colleagues across intelligence, analytics, and account management to support development of deliverables and client-facing work. Develop clear tables, charts, written summaries, and presentation slides that communicate findings to healthcare strategy leaders and other audiences. Participate in team meetings, learning sessions, and selected client and internal discussions; track project milestones and incorporate feedback. What You’ll Learn Key trends and issues that matter to health system strategy and service line leaders and the industry more broadly; how demand, care delivery, and strategic priorities are evolving. How Strategy Intelligence and its membership are using data sources such as the Impact of Change forecast, claims products, consumer surveys, clinical and performance data to inform strategic decisions and program planning. Practical application of healthcare research, market and utilization analysis, forecasting concepts, and development of client-ready presentations and other intelligence. How clinical and enterprise subject-matter experts, cross-Vizient colleagues, and account teams combine perspectives to support health system strategy and client priorities. How to synthesize complex information, communicate a data-driven point of view, manage a scoped project, and tell a concise story for an executive audience. Qualifications Currently pursuing a graduate degree in healthcare administration, public health, business administration, health policy, economics, biological sciences, or a related field. Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint; experience organizing, analyzing, or presenting data is expected. PowerBI or DataBricks experience is preferred. Coursework or experience in healthcare management/administration, biological/biomedical sciences, economics, or a related area Ability to evaluate sources, synthesize information, identify meaningful findings, and communicate clearly in writing and in presentations. Demonstrated interest in healthcare delivery, health system strategy, clinical service lines, or the business of healthcare. Ability to work in a hybrid environment and participate in the Vizient internship program schedule, including the in-person Chicago orientation and other required program activities.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Internship - Research Analytics & Insights (Graduate/Doctorate Level) at Vizient, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Vizient, Inc. Expires: 12/07/2026 Vizient Intern Program Overview: This program is designed to foster a beneficial relationship and provide growth opportunities for Vizient, our employees, and collegiate students. Since 2000, our summer intern program has provided college undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students with practical experience that exposes them to multiple aspects of a career field and the healthcare industry. This full-time, paid intern program offers an opportunity to accelerate academic learning, apply classroom knowledge, and introduce students to a professional setting. Interns are assigned a supervisor to mentor/develop their business skills, as well as monitor their work experiences. Interns are integral members of the company’s team, setting goals, working toward deadlines, and actively participating in community service projects. The program requires the intern to commit to 10 weeks of participation in all formal training, mentoring, on-the-job learning, and opportunities to interact with senior leaders. Program starts June 1, 2027, and ends August 6, 2027 Pay rate: $25 per hour. About the team and role The Research Analytics & Insights (RAIN) team uses Vizient data and research methods to generate evidence and insights that help healthcare organizations understand performance, quality outcomes, and emerging industry questions. The team supports internal research priorities and member-focused analyses by combining background research, thoughtful study design, data analysis, and clear communication of findings. The intern will receive hands-on training in the Vizient Clinical Data Base (CDB) and contribute to a defined healthcare analytics project. Working with the RAIN team, the intern will develop an analytic question, identify relevant data and literature, conduct and interpret analyses, and translate findings into a concise final presentation or research deliverable. What You’ll Do Complete training in the Vizient CDB online tool and use its front-end interface to support healthcare data analysis. Contribute to a defined research or analytics project addressing a RAIN team priority or client-relevant healthcare question. Conduct focused literature and background research, refine analytic questions, and identify appropriate measures and datasets. Perform data extraction, validation, descriptive analysis, and interpretation to identify meaningful trends and insights. Collaborate with RAIN colleagues and cross-functional partners to review methods, findings, and implications. Develop clear documentation, visualizations, and a final presentation or written research deliverable for technical and nontechnical audiences. Support updates to internal SharePoint content and team knowledge resources, as needed. What You’ll Learn How healthcare data and research are used to evaluate quality, utilization, outcomes, and performance. Practical use of administrative claims-based data and a structured workflow for moving from a research question to an analytic result. Methods for literature review, measure definition, data validation, interpretation, and responsible communication of findings. How research and analytics teams partner with internal stakeholders and healthcare organizations. Professional skills in project planning, data storytelling, presentation development, and stakeholder communication. Qualifications Currently pursuing a master’s or doctoral degree in health services research, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, health informatics, healthcare administration, or a related quantitative field; an undergraduate degree must be completed before the internship begins. Coursework or applied experience in quantitative research methods, statistics, healthcare analytics, or study design. Experience using at least one analytic tool or language, such as SQL, Python, R, SAS, Excel, Power BI, or Tableau, through coursework, research, employment, or a prior internship. Demonstrated experience working with data, including cleaning or validating data, conducting analysis, interpreting results, and communicating findings. Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage a defined project and collaborate in a hybrid team environment. Interest in healthcare quality, outcomes, utilization, or health services research.

jobs.title: AmeriCorps Summer Teaching Fellow at SSC Learning Network
jobs.description: Employer: SSC Learning Network Expires: 12/08/2026 About Breakthrough Silicon ValleyBreakthrough Silicon Valley launches talented students who have been historically excluded from higher education on the path to college, and inspires high school and college students to become the next generation of leaders, advocates, and educators. BTSV’s six -year college access and success program, which supports students from 7th grade to first year of college, has proven to be effective in preparing these students for college: a stunning 99% of BTSV graduates attend college immediately after high school. BTSV’s tuition-free program provides year-round out-of-school time academic support, advising, and advocacy for a diverse group of talented students, most of whom come from under-resourced communities and will be the first generation in their family to go to college. Through our students-teaching-students model, BTSV also provides a consummate professional development experience providing talented high school and college students the opportunity to understand the K-12 system and the drivers of educational inequities, and to design and teach classes under the direction of seasoned educators. Located in San Jose, California, Breakthrough Silicon Valley is an affiliate of The Breakthrough Collaborative, a leading national service organization that acts as the national voice for 25 Breakthrough sites across the country. About the Summer Teaching FellowshipYour Impact: Our summer program could not be what it is every year without the dedicated service of our Teaching Fellows. You won’t just be a teacher. You’ll be a mentor and a role model to your students. You will witness how your leadership helps your students grow personally and progress academically in just a few weeks. What does a typical summer look like?Pre-Service Orientation TrainingYour journey begins with an immersive Pre-Service Orientation. During the first few days, you'll dive into the essentials of lesson planning, instructional strategies, and classroom management techniques. Alongside other AmeriCorps Teaching Fellows, you’ll build connections, form lasting friendships, and become familiar with Breakthrough's vibrant culture and mission. During this time, you’ll meet your Instructional Coach, a seasoned educator in your subject area, who will mentor you throughout the summer. This guidance will set the foundation for your success in the classroom.The Summer Program ExperienceTeaching Fellows are responsible for delivering engaging instruction in core academic subjects such as reading, writing, math, and science, as well as leading elective classes that inspire and motivate middle school students. In addition, Fellows serve as Crew Leaders, fostering community and building relationships through daily crew time by planning and facilitating icebreakers, energizers, and team-building activities. Fellows serve closely with an Instructional Coach, participating in regular meetings to strengthen their teaching and leadership skills while incorporating feedback to support continuous professional growth as educators.But it's not all work! Breakthrough’s summer is packed with joy-filled traditions like college campus visits, the summer talent show, Spirit Week, field days, and the Breakthrough Olympics. You’ll not only help students learn but also build a community of fun, encouragement, and support that will leave a lasting impact.Wrap-Up Week and Reflecting on Your ImpactAt the end of the summer, you'll celebrate the achievements of your students and reflect on the incredible growth you’ve witnessed in them—and yourself. Wrap-Up Week provides time to document these experiences and share your insights. It also offers career-building opportunities through panels featuring local professionals in fields like counseling, educational technology, higher education, and youth development. These sessions will help you envision your next steps as a future leader in education or beyond.This journey will not only give you hands-on teaching experience but also prepare you for a meaningful career, surrounded by a community that celebrates growth, learning, and the joy of teaching. Mentorship and GuidanceYou will serve under the mentorship of an experienced Instructional Coach, who will review your lesson plans, provide daily feedback, and train you in effective teaching strategies, classroom management, and student assessment techniques. Teaching Fellows will receive their Performance Review at the conclusion of their service. The final performance review will also include:Whether the member has completed the required number of hoursWhether the member has satisfactorily completed assignmentsWhether the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service and in the member's position description.Ideal CandidateThis position is perfect for you if:You are passionate about serving with middle- and high-school students.You are eager to tackle a steep learning curve with enthusiasm and an open mind.You pride yourself on your organizational skills and attention to detail.You are looking to start a career in education, social justice, or public service.You enjoy laughter and having fun while making a difference.You can commit to 300+ hours of service from June 14 to August 6, 2027, serving full-time hours throughout the program.Embark on a summer journey that will not only enrich your professional skills but also leave a lasting impact on the lives of young students. Join us as a Teaching Fellow and make this summer unforgettable! Training and Professional DevelopmentBTSV wants you to learn and grow as much as your students will. At the start of your service, you will receive a comprehensive orientation to your new team, to BTSV, our program, and your role. Throughout the summer program you will serve with your colleagues, BTSV Staff, and with the expert guidance of an Instructional Coach, an experienced educator who will provide training, coaching, observation, feedback, encouragement, and support. Members will receive formal and structured feedback via performance reviews. Note, training hours will not exceed 20% of total service hours. Requirements“Breakthrough Spirit”: You’re a collaborative team player who is committed to excellence and is open-minded. You demonstrate a growth mindset, think creatively to solve problems, and serve with a sense of humor and humility.Commitment to Breakthrough Silicon Valley’s mission and goals as well as a passion for educational equity.Have a commitment to community service and the ability to serve the full service term. (300+ hrs of service, full-time from June 14 to August 6, 2027)Recent college graduate, or currently enrolled in college or high school.At least 17 years old at the start of the service period (June 14, 2027).Candidates 18 years of age or older must pass a National Service Criminal History Check.US citizen, US national, or lawful permanent resident of the United States.Access to reliable transportation to our summer program sites via personal vehicle, public transit, or other means.Spanish or Vietnamese language skills are a plus, but not required. Compensation & BenefitsAmeriCorps positions are volunteer roles which carry a living allowance. BTSV’s AmeriCorps Members will receive:$5,294 living allowance (pre-tax) paid semi-monthly over the service period.Summer Teaching Fellows who complete their AmeriCorps service are eligible for a $1,565.08 education award via the Segal AmeriCorps Education Award. This can be used for continuing education or to repay certain student loans.Student loan forbearance, if eligible. Location(s)BTSV maintains two offices in San Jose and our Summer Program sites will be co-located or nearby to these offices:Bridges Academy: 1702 McLaughlin Ave, San Jose, CA 95122Herbert Hoover Middle School: 1635 Park Ave, San Jose, CA 95126 Teaching Fellows are required to serve full-time in person. This is not a remote position. Application ProcessApply online at http://breakthroughsv.org/becomeateachingfellow. We will review applications on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: College Intern - Resort Operations at Marriott Vacations Worldwide
jobs.description: Employer: Marriott Vacations Worldwide Expires: 12/10/2026 Internship Program Overview Marriott Vacations Worldwide offers a comprehensive internship program at one of our stunning resort locations, available in 3- or 6-month durations, and built around the following core pillars: Gain in-person, on-site work experience within a designated department at one of our premier resort locations. Join interactive online sessions designed to provide exposure to various areas of the MVW business. Connect with fellow interns and share your journey through our dedicated internship social media platform.
